records.statement: Stock shock spring rate: 54 N/mm on the {y} RM-Z450, as listed by magazine and tester setup sheets (not from a Suzuki-published source). One 2023 spec table and one owner's-manual copy list 56 N/mm instead, so check the marking on the spring before ordering a different rate.
records.notes: Dirt Rider 2025 lists 54 and says the shock spring rate has been the same since 2019; Keefer 2025 and 2026 baselines use 54. Dirt Rider 2023 and a later manual copy list 56.

records.statement: Tester baseline for the {y} RM-Z450 (Keefer Inc Testing, stock valving): fork 5.0 N/mm springs, fork height 3-5 mm up in the clamps, compression 9 clicks out, rebound 14 clicks out; shock 54 N/mm spring, race sag 105 mm, compression 1.25 turns out, rebound 1.5 turns out. The BFRC shock has one compression adjuster (no separate high-speed).
records.notes: Same tester, 2025 and 2026 articles; the 2026 article says the setting has not changed. A tester's setting, not the factory standard.

records.statement: Model history as reported by magazine tests: the current RM-Z450 arrived for 2018, got a softer shock spring for 2019, and was mechanically unchanged from 2020 through 2025 (changes were graphics and editions). A tester's 2026 baseline says his settings did not change from 2025. Setup advice and parts for any 2019-2026 RM-Z450 generally carry across those years.
records.notes: MXA 2025: unchanged 2020-2024, no changes for 2025. Dirt Rider 2023: 2019-2022 revisions strictly cosmetic, 2023 completely unchanged. Dirt Rider 2025: last mechanical revisions 2019.

records.statement: Testers report the stock clutch on the RM-Z450 slips under hard use; the common fix they give is stiffer (heavier) clutch springs.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2025 race test; the bike is mechanically unchanged 2020-2025.

records.statement: Testers report the RM-Z450 can lose coolant in long motos. They list the stock radiator cap at 1.1 kg/cm2 and fit a higher-pressure cap (1.8 to 2.0 kg/cm2) to stop it.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2025 race test.

records.statement: Stock gearing is 13/50. Motocross Action ran 13/51 (one tooth more on the rear) to help the engine pull, and short-shifted to keep it between about 7,000 and 8,800 rpm because power falls off above about 9,000 rpm.
records.notes: Stock 13/50 is listed by both Motocross Action and Dirt Rider (2025); 13/51 is Motocross Action's choice.

records.statement: Testers describe the stock Showa BFRC shock as harsh over consecutive bumps and prone to a rebound kick, and the stock fork as worth a re-valve. Motocross Action ran the fork flush with the top of the clamps and a longer aftermarket shock linkage to lower the rear and calm headshake.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2025 race test; opinion of one test crew.

records.statement: Measured by Dirt Rider on a 2023 RM-Z450: 50.9 hp at 8,500 rpm and 33.7 lb-ft at 7,300 rpm on their dyno; 251 lb wet with a full tank; seat height 37.1 in; stock header and muffler 9.2 lb.
records.notes: One magazine's dyno and scale; dyno numbers differ between dynos.

records.statement: Measured on 2025 RM-Z450 test bikes: Dirt Rider 52.8 hp at 9,100 rpm and 33.9 lb-ft at 7,100 rpm, 250 lb wet; Motocross Action 241 lb without fuel. Dyno numbers differ between dynos.
records.notes: Two magazines, each on its own dyno and scale.

records.topic: suspension, brakes and tires as tested
records.statement: As listed for the unchanged 2019-2025 RM-Z450 by Dirt Rider: Showa 49 mm coil-spring fork (12.0 in travel) and Showa BFRC shock (12.3 in travel); Nissin brakes with 270 mm front and 240 mm rear discs; Bridgestone Battlecross X30 tires, 80/100-21 front and 110/90-19 rear; wheelbase 58.3 in; rake 27.8 degrees, trail 4.7 in; 1.7 gal tank.
records.notes: Same figures in the 2023 and 2025 spec tables; magazines report no mechanical change 2020-2025.

records.statement: The RM-Z450 comes with three plug-in fuel couplers (stock, aggressive, mellow). Maps can also be changed with Suzuki's MX-Tuner phone app; testers note it needs an external battery to power the bike's electronics while tuning because the bike has no battery.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2025 race test.

records.statement: The 2027 RM-Z450 is not the same bike as 2018-2026 underneath: Suzuki lists a KYB coil-spring fork and KYB shock with new settings in place of the Showa fork and BFRC shock, new RK Excel rims, a revised intake port, a straighter handlebar bend and MX-Tuner 4.0; a magazine first look adds a new upper triple clamp and a new muffler on a narrower subframe. Clicker settings, sag and spring rates published for 2018-2026 bikes do not apply to the 2027 suspension.
records.notes: Suzuki's own 2027 model page plus two magazine reports. No public stock clicker or spring figures for the 2027 KYB parts were found as of 2026-11-20.

records.statement: Model history as reported by Motocross Action: the current RM-Z250 arrived for 2019 (new frame, KYB coil-spring fork, larger front brake rotor, dual injectors, new shock, revised cylinder head and gear ratios) and had no mechanical changes through 2025. Setup advice and parts for any 2019-2025 RM-Z250 generally carry across those years.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2024 and 2025 race tests (one publication).

records.topic: fork too stiff for most riders
records.statement: Testers find the stock 5.0 N/mm fork springs and valving too stiff for most 250 riders. Motocross Action's quick fix is lowering the fork oil level by 30 mm in each leg; the fuller fix they give is softer springs and a re-valve.
records.notes: Same advice in the 2024 and 2025 race tests (one publication).

records.statement: Reported by Motocross Action on the RM-Z250: the clutch starts to slip after a few hours (fix: stiffer aftermarket clutch springs); the front brake lacks power and fades; the aluminium frame feels rigid (they fitted aftermarket engine mounts); shifting is notchy under load; and with no electric start a stall costs time.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2025 race test; opinion of one test crew.

records.statement: Measured by Motocross Action on RM-Z250 test bikes: 227 lb without fuel (2024 and 2025); 39.52 peak hp on their dyno (2025), the lowest in the class. Testers short-shift it to stay in the mid-range.
records.notes: One magazine's dyno and scale.

records.statement: The RM-Z250 comes with three plug-in fuel couplers; testers say the white one is the most aggressive off the bottom. Suzuki's MX-Tuner 2.0 phone app adds four preset maps (aggressive, smooth, richer, leaner) and custom fuel and ignition maps; it needs a separately sold battery and cable to power the ECU. Motocross Action preferred Pro Circuit's map over stock.
records.notes: 2024 and 2025 race tests (one publication).

records.notes: Single manual copy; no second independent match found.

records.topic: fork oil quantity range and type
records.statement: Fork oil quantity adjustable range: 310-375 ml per leg; fork oil Suzuki L-05 or equivalent, as listed in a third-party copy of the 2019+ RM-Z250 owner's manual (one source; not from a Suzuki-published document, so treat as a starting point and verify).
records.notes: Single manual copy; no second independent match found.

records.statement: The 2027 RM-Z250 has new KYB fork and shock settings (both fork legs now carry the same springs and damping parts), new Excel rims with Dunlop Geomax MX34 tires, a new quieter muffler, subframe rails moved to fit a larger air cleaner, and footpegs and grips moved slightly; listed at 233 lb wet with a 58.5 in wheelbase and 37.6 in seat. Clicker settings and oil levels published for 2019-2026 bikes may not suit the 2027 suspension.
records.notes: Two magazine reports of Suzuki's 2027 announcement. No public stock clicker figures for the 2027 settings were found as of 2026-11-20.

records.topic: stock clicker positions and sag as listed by testers
records.statement: Stock positions for the {y} RM-Z450 as printed in Motocross Action setup sheets (not from a Suzuki-published source): fork compression 6 clicks out, shock compression 1.5 turns out, shock rebound 3 turns out, race sag 108 mm. Sources disagree: their 2022 sheet prints 12 clicks for the fork, and one owner's-manual copy of unknown year lists fork 9 clicks, shock 2 turns and 1 turn, and 110 mm sag. Write down where your own adjusters are before changing anything.
records.notes: One publication repeating its stock box 2021-2023; conflicts noted in the statement.

records.statement: Motocross Action race setting for the {y} RM-Z450 (stock valving): fork 5.0 N/mm springs, compression 10 clicks out (they ran 7 to 12 depending on rider speed and track), rebound 12 clicks out, fork height set for handling; shock 54 N/mm spring, race sag 105 mm, compression 1 turn out, rebound 1 turn out, with a 1 mm longer shock linkage to lower the rear. On the 2021 bike they also added 10 cc of oil to each fork leg to stop bottoming.
records.notes: Same test crew, three model years. A magazine's setting, not the factory standard.

records.statement: Motocross Action reports the stock chain guide on the RM-Z450 wears quickly and replaces it with an aftermarket guide. Check it for wear at every chain adjustment.
records.notes: Motocross Action 2021 race test; the bike is mechanically unchanged 2020-2025.

records.statement: Measured by Motocross Action on the {y} RM-Z450: 54.39 peak hp at 8,800 rpm on their dyno; 241 lb without fuel.
records.notes: One magazine's dyno and scale; dyno numbers differ between dynos.

records.statement: Measured by Motocross Action on the 2024 RM-Z450 (with the edition's Pro Circuit exhaust): 56.7 peak hp at 9,000 rpm on their dyno; 241 lb without fuel.
